sections.heading: The budget — constitutional identity and structure

blocks.text: The budget is constitutionally the **Annual Financial Statement (Art 112** for the Union; **Art 202** for states**)** — the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government for the financial year, laid before the legislature. Money flows through three constitutional funds: the **Consolidated Fund (Art 266(1))** — all revenues, loans and receipts, withdrawable only by appropriation law; the **Contingency Fund (Art 267)** — imprest for unforeseen expenditure (Union corpus raised to **₹30,000 crore**, 2021), recouped later; and the **Public Account (Art 266(2))** — money held in trust (provident funds, small savings), no appropriation needed.

rows: **Tax revenue** (direct: income, corporate; indirect: GST, customs, excise) + **non-tax** (dividends incl. RBI surplus, interest, spectrum fees)
Salaries, pensions, **interest payments** (largest single head), subsidies (food-fertiliser-LPG), grants to states (even for capital creation — an accounting quirk)
Borrowings (market loans), **disinvestment receipts**, recovery of loans
**Capital expenditure**: infrastructure, machinery, loans to states (incl. 50-yr interest-free capex loans), equity injections

items: **Charged vs voted**: charged expenditure (President/judges' salaries, interest, CAG) is **non-votable** (Art 112(3)) — discussed but not put to vote; the rest needs demands-for-grants approval.

**Documents ecosystem**: AFS, Demands for Grants, Finance Bill, **FRBM statements** (Macro-Economic Framework, Medium-Term Fiscal Policy), Expenditure Profile/Budget at a Glance, **Output-Outcome Framework**, and the Economic Survey (a day earlier, by CEA).

**Revenue vs capital** — the quality-of-spending lens: revenue expenditure consumes, capex creates assets with multiplier ~2.5–4x vs ~<1 for revenue transfers (RBI/NIPFP estimates) — the intellectual basis of the post-2020 capex push.
**Plan vs non-plan abolished (2017-18)** on Rangarajan committee logic; replaced by revenue-capital across all heads — a favourite prelims trap.
**Scheme lens**: Central Sector (100% Centre) vs **Centrally Sponsored** (shared, states implement) vs Finance-Commission transfers vs states' own schemes.
**Gender/child/SC-ST budgeting**: cross-cutting statements tagging allocations (gender budget ~1% of GDP scale) — welfare-targeting lenses.
**Merger reforms**: Railway budget merged (2017, Bibek Debroy panel); budget date advanced to **1 February** (2017) so allocations operate from 1 April; paperless budget since 2021.

items: The state budget mirrors the Union constitutionally (**Arts 202–207**): AP's AFS, its Consolidated Fund, charged items (Governor, HC judges' salaries), Appropriation Acts in the Assembly; AP presents gender and welfare annexures and (like most states) a **Socio-Economic Survey** alongside.

**AP structural signature** (link to RMA-012): revenue expenditure dominance — welfare DBT + salaries/pensions/interest leave capex ~10-12% of total spend in tight years — the 'quality of expenditure' critique made concrete.

Craft: for 'structure & components', draw the three-funds + two-accounts diagram, then the charged/voted and revenue/capital distinctions with one number each (₹30,000 cr contingency; capex multiplier) — precision over length.

blocks.text: Exam tip: Four articles (112, 266, 267, 114), two accounts, three funds, one multiplier — that's the complete skeleton. The revenue-vs-capital quality argument converts a descriptive question into an analytical answer.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the budget's constitutional anatomy

rows: The 'Budget' — receipts & expenditure of a year
All revenues; withdrawals need parliamentary appropriation
Provident funds, small savings — no appropriation needed
At the President's disposal for unforeseen expenditure

blocks.text: **Classification lenses examiners test:** Revenue vs Capital budget; Plan vs Non-plan (**abolished from 2017-18** — now Revenue/Capital only); developmental vs non-developmental; the shift to **outcome budgeting** and the merger of the Railway Budget (2017) and advancing the date to **1 February**. **AP mirror:** the same architecture under the AP Financial Code, presented by the state Finance Minister.

prelimsPointers: **Annual Financial Statement (Art 112)** is the constitutional term for the Budget.
**Plan/Non-plan** distinction **abolished** from the 2017-18 budget; Railway Budget merged the same year.
**Charged expenditure** is non-votable (e.g., salaries of SC/HC judges, CAG, interest on debt).
'Budget' appears nowhere in the Constitution — the term is **Annual Financial Statement (Art 112)**.
**Art 266(1)** Consolidated Fund; **Art 267** Contingency Fund (Union corpus **₹30,000 crore** since 2021-22, held by Finance Secretary); **Art 266(2)** Public Account.
**Charged expenditure** (Art 112(3)): President's emoluments, judges' salaries & pensions, CAG, interest/debt — non-votable.
No tax except by authority of law — **Art 265**; withdrawal from CFI only via **Appropriation Act (Art 114)**.
**Plan/non-plan distinction abolished 2017-18**; Railway budget merged 2017; budget date advanced to **1 Feb**.
Interest payments are the **largest expenditure head** of the Union revenue account.
Capex multiplier estimated ~**2.5–4x**, far above revenue-expenditure multipliers — basis of the capex strategy.

glossary.definition: The constitutionally mandated statement of estimated receipts and expenditure (Arts 112/202) — the budget's legal identity.
The single pool of all government revenues, borrowings and receipts, withdrawable only under appropriation law.
Trust monies (provident funds, small savings) the government holds as banker — spendable without legislative vote.
Constitutionally protected spending (judges, CAG, interest) not submitted to the House's vote — insulating institutions from majority pressure.
Spending that creates assets or reduces liabilities — infrastructure, equipment, loans — the growth-multiplying half of the budget.
Statement mapping outlays to measurable outputs and outcomes per scheme — the results lens on allocations.

blocks.text: Budgeting runs an annual **cycle of four stages**: **formulation** (Sept–Jan: Budget Division circular, ministries' estimates, RE/BE finalisation, pre-budget consultations, the **halwa ceremony** & lock-in), **enactment** (presentation 1 Feb → general discussion → **DRSC scrutiny of demands** → discussion & voting of demands (LS only) → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill** (taxation; must pass in 75 days)), **execution** (funds release via **TSA/PFMS**, competent-authority sanctions, reappropriations), and **audit & review** (CAG audit → PAC examination → Action Taken — closing the loop ~2 years later).

rows: Advance grant (~2 months) to keep government running pending full passage — routine before elections/interim budgets
Policy cut (₹1), economy cut, token cut (₹100) — symbolic accountability; fall of one = confidence crisis
Undiscussed demands voted en bloc on the last allotted day — in recent years the **vast majority of demands are guillotined**, the central critique of budget scrutiny
Mid-year additional needs; excess grants need PAC scrutiny post-facto
Appropriation authorises **spending** from CFI; Finance Act authorises **taxation** — both money bills (Art 110)

items: **Calendar & format**: date advanced to **1 Feb (2017)** enabling full-year execution; **railway merger (2017)**; **plan/non-plan abolition (2017-18)**; **paperless budget + Union Budget app (2021)**; halwa-to-lock-in continuity.
**Fund-flow re-engineering**: **PFMS 'just-in-time' releases**, **SNA (2021)** for CSS (ending float parking), **TSA** for autonomous bodies — treasury efficiency worth crores in interest.
**Results orientation**: **Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework** covering major schemes; NITI's DMEO evaluations; gender/child/SC-ST statements; climate-tagging experiments.
**Fiscal transparency**: post-2021 budgets brought **off-budget borrowings (FCI loans etc.) above the line** — a credibility reform (the 'honest budget' point); FRBM statements give rolling targets.

**Frontier critiques & fixes**: guillotine culture (fix: mandatory minimum discussion days; a **parliamentary budget office** for independent costing), RE-BE gaming, single-year horizon (fix: medium-term expenditure frameworks with teeth), execution rigidity (fix: flexi-funds within CSS), and weak post-legislative scrutiny (fix: PAC capacity + timely Action-Taken).

sections.heading: AP process notes and answer craft

items: AP mirrors the cycle in the Assembly (**Arts 202–207**): Governor's recommendation, demands by department, Appropriation & Finance Acts; with a **Legislative Council**, money bills follow the RS-like 14-day limitation (Art 198). AP has run **vote-on-account budgets in election years** (2019, 2024) — live examples of Art 116's state counterpart.

Craft: narrate the four stages in one line each, then spend the answer on **evaluation** — guillotine data, DRSC referral decline, PFMS/SNA gains, off-budget cleanup — process questions are actually accountability questions.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'Recent changes' = the 2017 trio (date, railway, plan) + 2021 trio (paperless, off-budget honesty, SNA/JIT) — six reforms with one line each is a complete 10-marker. Add the parliamentary-budget-office suggestion to end forward-looking.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — the budget cycle & parliamentary control

items: **Four stages:** (1) **Preparation** (Finance Ministry + line ministries); (2) **Enactment** (presentation → general discussion → **Demands for Grants** → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill**); (3) **Execution**; (4) **Audit** (CAG → PAC).

**Parliamentary control tools:** **cut motions** (Policy/Disapproval, Economy, Token), **Vote on Account** (Art 116, now largely superseded by advancing the budget), **Guillotine** (undiscussed demands put to vote together), and the **Departmentally Related Standing Committees** that scrutinise demands.
**Post-audit:** the **CAG (Art 148)** audits; the **Public Accounts Committee**, **Estimates Committee** and **Committee on Public Undertakings** complete the accountability loop.
**Reform frontier:** outcome budgeting, gender & child budgeting, zero-based review of schemes, and greater transparency on off-budget borrowings.

prelimsPointers: **Cut motions**: Disapproval of Policy (₹1), Economy, and Token (₹100).
**Guillotine** — remaining demands for grants are voted without discussion at a set time.
**Appropriation Bill** authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund; **Finance Bill** enacts tax proposals.
Budget presented on **1 February** since 2017 (earlier: last working day of Feb); Economic Survey precedes it.
**Vote on account: Art 116** — typically two months' expenditure (1/6 of estimates).
**Finance Bill must be passed within 75 days** of introduction (Provisional Collection of Taxes framework).
Demands for grants are voted **only by the Lok Sabha** (Art 113); Rajya Sabha discusses.
**26 Departmentally Related Standing Committees**-era scrutiny: demands referred after general discussion, House in recess.
**SNA (2021)/PFMS**: CSS funds tracked; just-in-time release reforms cut idle float.
**Off-budget FCI borrowings (NSSF loans)** were brought on-budget in the FY22 budget — transparency landmark.
Excess grants (Art 115) require **PAC** examination before regularisation.

glossary.definition: Parliament's advance grant for a short period pending full budget passage — expenditure continuity without policy change.
En-bloc voting of all outstanding demands when allotted time ends — the symbol of shrinking budget scrutiny.
The law authorising withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund for voted and charged expenditure — spending's legal gate.
Mid-year re-projection of the current year's receipts/spending presented with the next budget — the BE-RE-Actuals credibility chain.
Transferring funds only when implementing agencies actually need to pay — ending idle balances that cost interest.

sections.heading: Types of budget — the philosophy menu

rows: Modern welfare states run counter-cyclical deficits (Keynes); chronic structural deficits are the disease
Strong control, blind to results — still the Indian base layer
Link inputs to outputs (1st Hoover Commission; India from 1968)
Analytically elegant, administratively heavy — faded globally
Justify every rupee afresh each year (Pyhrr; India experiments 1986-87)
Ideal against incrementalism; too costly to do annually — used selectively for scheme reviews/sunsets
Outlays → outputs → outcomes with indicators (India 2005-06 onwards)
The current Indian frame; measurement quality is its weak spot
Tag and design allocations by gender impact (India since 2005-06)
~1% of GDP tagged; Part A/B statements; quality-over-quantity critique

blocks.text: **Revenue deficit** = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts (living beyond current means). **Effective revenue deficit** = RD − grants to states for capital creation. **Fiscal deficit** = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts) = **the year's borrowing requirement** — the headline number. **Primary deficit** = FD − interest payments (this year's fresh fiscal behaviour, stripped of past debt's cost). Financing: market borrowings (dated securities + T-bills), small savings (NSSF), external debt (~1–2%, lowest among peers), and — barred since FRBM — direct monetisation (RBI primary subscriptions; the WMA window remains for cash mismatches).

items: **FRBM discipline**: Act 2003; **2018 amendments (post-N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee)** — fiscal-deficit anchor **3% of GDP**, **debt targets: Centre 40% / general government 60%**, escape clause (0.5%, invoked COVID); revenue-deficit target dropped as an operational anchor.

**The COVID arc**: Union FD spiked to **9.2% (FY21)** → glide path announced to **below 4.5% by FY26** — met in stages (5.6% FY24, ~4.8-4.9% FY25 RE, ~4.4% FY26 BE); the new anchor from FY27: **debt-to-GDP path** (Centre ~50% by 2031 direction) rather than annual FD points — a conceptual shift worth citing.

**Management toolkit**: expenditure quality (capex share up), revenue buoyancy (GST maturation, direct-tax simplification), asset monetisation & disinvestment (chronic under-achievement), subsidy rationalisation (DBT-LPG, urea neem-coating), and honest accounting (off-budget cleanup).

**Deficit-debate balance**: austerity vs growth — deficits that fund capex with high multipliers can be **self-stabilising** (growth denominator); deficits funding current transfers risk debt spirals when **r > g**; India's saving grace: domestic-currency, domestically-held debt.

items: **State FRBM**: net borrowing ceiling ~**3% of GSDP** (+0.5% power-reform incentive); AP typically seeks full ceilings, runs **revenue deficits** (the structurally 'bad' kind), and has faced ceiling deductions for past off-budget borrowings — the state is the national deficit-quality debate in miniature.

Craft: define the four deficits with formulas → FRBM targets and the FY21-FY26 arc → the debt-anchor shift → quality-of-deficit argument → AP mirror. Numbers: 3%, 40/60, 9.2% (FY21), 4.5% (FY26 target).

blocks.text: Exam tip: Examiners test whether you know WHICH deficit measures what: FD = borrowing, RD = consumption financing, PD = current-year behaviour. The 'not all deficits are equal' composition argument + the new debt-anchor shift are the analysis that tops answers.

sections.heading: 💰 Deep mastery — budget philosophies & the deficit hierarchy

rows: Government borrowing to meet consumption — a red flag
The 'fresh' fiscal gap net of past debt servicing
Revenue deficit − grants for capital assets
Introduced to isolate genuine consumption borrowing

blocks.text: **Budget philosophies:** balanced, deficit (Keynesian counter-cyclical), surplus, **zero-based**, **performance/outcome**, and **gender budgeting**. The **FRBM Act (2003, amended 2018)** sets the discipline; the **N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee** recommended a **debt-to-GDP anchor (60% general govt: 40% Centre, 20% states)** with fiscal deficit as the operational target. **AP mirror:** the AP FRBM Act binds the state to similar ceilings.

prelimsPointers: **Primary deficit** = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments.
**FRBM Review Committee (N.K. Singh)** — recommended a debt-to-GDP anchor of 60% (40% Centre + 20% States).
**Zero-based budgeting** — every expenditure justified afresh each year (from zero).
**Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts)** — equals gross borrowing requirement.
**Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments**.
FRBM Act **2003**; 2018 amendment: FD anchor **3%**, debt **40% Centre / 60% general government**, **escape clause ±0.5%**.
Union FD: **9.2% (FY21)** → glide path **< 4.5% by FY26**; from FY27 the anchor shifts to a **declining debt-GDP ratio**.
**Zero-based budgeting**: Peter Pyhrr (Texas Instruments); Indian experiments from 1986-87.
**Gender budgeting** statement since **2005-06** (Part A: women-specific 100%; Part B: ≥30% allocations).
States' net borrowing ceiling: **3% of GSDP** + 0.5% power-sector-reform linked (recent norms).
**Effective revenue deficit** excludes grants to states used for capital creation — introduced 2011-12.

glossary.definition: The excess of total expenditure over non-borrowed receipts — the government's borrowing requirement and the headline fiscal indicator.
Borrowing used to finance current consumption (revenue spending beyond revenue receipts) — the quality-negative deficit.
Fiscal deficit net of interest — isolating the current year's discretionary fiscal stance from inherited debt costs.
FRBM provision allowing deviation up to 0.5% of GDP on specified grounds (war, calamity, structural reform) with stated return path.
Medium-term debt-to-GDP target replacing annual deficit points as the fiscal rule — the post-FY26 Indian framework.
Central bank financing of government deficits by primary subscription — barred under FRBM to protect price stability.
